newsitem.title: USA: L.A. County may face court funding shortfall - CAO.
newsitem.headline: L.A. County may face court funding shortfall - CAO.

text.p: Los Angeles County's chief administrative officer warned Thursday that the county could face a $100 million shortfall as a result of the state Legislature's failure to approve court funding legislation.

Chief Administrator David Janssen said in a letter to county supervisors that the county could face a $90 to $100 million shortfall if the Legislature does not take steps to address the court funding issue.
Legislation by state Assemblyman Phil Isenberg would have overhauled court financing and provided counties with certainty for future funding of the courts.
But the measure was not taken up by the Assembly.

The shortfall would occur because there will be no new revenues for the courts from various fee increases and no statutory authority to allocate fine and forfeiture revenues to pay for court operations.
As a result, courts may face a budget shortfall of close to $300 million statewide, according to the California state Association of Counties.
Janssen said a technical correction would be needed to appropriate and allocate fines and forfeitures revenue back to counties.
